title: G7 leaders agree on 50 billion dollar ERA loans for Ukraine backed by Russian asset revenues
body:
On 25 October 2024, G7 leaders issued a statement saying they had "reached a consensus on how to deliver approximately $50 billion" in Extraordinary Revenue Acceleration (ERA) loans to Ukraine. The loans are to be serviced and repaid from future extraordinary revenues generated by the immobilisation of Russian sovereign assets, in line with each G7 member's legal system and international law. The principal of the frozen assets is not itself confiscated under the scheme.

Disbursements were to go through multiple channels to support Ukraine's budget, military and reconstruction needs, with the stated aim of beginning disbursement by the end of 2024. The statement said: "Time is not on President Putin's side."

The European Union's contribution was approved two days earlier. On 23 October 2024, the European Council approved by written procedure a 35 billion euro macro-financial loan to Ukraine, to be paid and serviced from the extraordinary proceeds of Russian assets frozen in the EU. Other reporting indicated that the remainder of the 50 billion dollars was to come from the United States, the United Kingdom, Canada and Japan, though the split was not set out in the G7 statement as quoted. The ERA mechanism followed earlier EU decisions in 2024 to channel windfall profits from immobilised Russian central bank assets to Ukraine.
